Chapter 4: Overcoming Obstacles and Embracing Flexibility in Prayer
Let’s be honest—while praying through the Bible sounds simple, it’s totally normal to run into questions or little roadblocks along the way. Maybe you’ve wondered, “Is it okay to skip a verse that doesn’t really connect?” Or maybe you worry you’re not praying the “right” way, or that your words just aren’t enough.
Here’s something that might surprise you: there’s a lot of freedom in this practice. You don’t need to follow a strict formula or check off every verse. The real goal? Just be honest. Show up as yourself. There’s no rule that says you have to pray about every single line, finish a passage, or use fancy words.
Think about it this way: if a verse doesn’t speak to you, it’s perfectly fine to move on. Why force it? Focus on what really tugs at your heart in that moment. And when it comes to the words you use, don’t worry about sticking exactly to the text. Let your own voice and feelings come through—that’s what makes your prayer real.
Maybe you only have a few minutes before work or while the kids are napping. That’s okay too. Even a short time spent praying through a passage can be deeply meaningful. And if you ever feel like your prayers aren’t “good enough,” remember this: God isn’t looking for perfection. He delights in sincere, honest conversation—no matter how simple or unfinished it might feel.
This kind of flexibility is actually key to keeping your prayer life vibrant. It takes away the pressure to perform and opens up space for a real, growing relationship. Praying the Bible isn’t about meeting some impossible standard—it’s about connecting with God, right where you are.
If you’re praying with others—maybe in a group or with family—you can adapt the method to fit your setting. One person might read a verse out loud, and others can respond with their own prayers. Or, you can take turns picking passages and sharing what stands out. You can make it as structured or as relaxed as you want.
Over time, this approach can really transform the way you see prayer. Instead of feeling like a duty or a box to check, it becomes a living conversation—one that’s constantly shaped by the words and stories you find in Scripture. And because the Bible is so rich and varied, no two prayer times ever have to be the same.
What about those moments when your mind drifts and you get distracted? The beauty of this method is that the text itself gently brings you back. The words of Scripture act like an anchor, helping you refocus and stay present in your conversation with God.
When you embrace this flexibility, you start to realize prayer isn’t about following rules—it’s about building a relationship. The Bible shifts from being just a book you study to a true companion on your faith journey. And as you keep practicing, you’ll find that prayer becomes more alive, bringing fresh depth and unexpected joy to your spiritual life.
